newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh flood toll at 39, many flee into hills.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh flood toll at 39, many flee into hills.

text.p: Floods sweeping Bangladesh have killed at least 39 people, including three buried under tonnes of mud on Saturday, and left a quarter of a million homeless, officials said.
At least half a million people were reported marooned in their half-submerged homes as the floods gripped 19 out of the country's 64 administrative districts.
Worst hit were 10 southeast districts including Chittagong, the Chittagong Hill Tracts and Cox's Bazar.
The latest deaths occurred in Banbarban district where water inundated an entire town, forcing thousands of residents to flee into surrounding hills.
"Civilians, police and military personnel all ran for (their) life. Many climbed on the hills and others were rushed to flood shelters," Bandarban journalist Munirul Islam said.
"Even some flood shelters were wrecked by torrents of rain water from the hills, and rescuers struggled to help out families huddled inside," he told Reuters.
Offices, business centres, police stations and army garrisons were evacuated, one Bandarban official said.
"Telecommunication with Bandarban (90 km from Chittagong) could break down anytime," a police wireless operator said.
Officials and police earlier said the victims of the floods, which started on Tuesday, died in landslides, house cave-ins and by drowning. At least 100 people have been injured, they said.
Unofficial sources on Saturday put the death toll at more than 50.
Weather officials said the floods could spread further and death counts could go up with more rains expected in next few days.
Heavy showers on Saturday disrupted life in the Bangladesh capital Dhaka, a city of nine million people, many of whom live in slums. Low areas on the city's outskirts were inundated.
More than 50,000 people were shifted to flood shelters and many more moved to higher ground on their own.
Road links between Chittagong and neighbouring districts, including Cox's Bazar, were reported impassable as floodwater washed away several small bridges and partly inundated highways.
Train communications at different sections of the affected areas were disrupted because tracks were flooded or under threat
Handling of cargo at the Chittagong port was hampered, port officials said. The national airline Bangladesh Biman said flights to and from Chittagong were delayed or suspended.
Movement of ships at Chittagong port became risky because of strong currents and waves at the Karnaphuli river linking the port to the Bay of Bengal.
Work at the country's second sea port at Mongla, in Khulna district, was also partially disrupted. Floodwaters have inundated at least 50 villages in the northeastern tea-growing district of Sylhet.
Road links between Sylhet and neighbouring districts were threatened by fast rising rivers and water rushing in from Indian hills across the broder.
At least 300,000 acres (120,000 hectares) of cropland have been inundated.
